messages:
sana: FYI starting bring-up for pelican-embed-v1, running int8 per-channel quant. want a quick sanity pass on recall@k + clustering stability before we push to staging. will run the usual multilingual holdout + short-query set.
matt: SGTM. do you want batch size / kv-cache toggles or default runtime config?
sana: default first. if recall drops > 3% vs prod baseline we stop and investigate. also check silhouette score for the topic clusters.
alexa: quick heads up — pelican has smaller dimensionality (384) vs our prod 512. expect nominal recall hit; curious about density tradeoffs with PQ/hnsw params.
jules: ran an initial sweep on en+es holdout just now. results attached below.
ci-bot: test-run 2056789150: embedding-eval/pelican-int8 -> completed
jules: ```
command: ./eval_embeddings --model pelican-embed-v1 --quant int8 --holdouts en,es --sets short_queries,wiki_top
metrics:
  recall@1: 0.712
  recall@5: 0.882
  recall@10: 0.921
  silhouette(topic_clusters): 0.27
  mean-dist-intra: 0.42
  mean-dist-inter: 0.63
notes: recall@1 down ~4.1% vs prod-512-fp16 baseline, recall@5 down ~1.5%.
```
sana: thanks. curious if the drop is concentrated on short queries or across all sets.
jules: short_queries recall@1 = 0.65 (down 6.2%), wiki_top recall@1 = 0.74 (down 2.0%). language split: es drop larger on short queries.
matt: can you rerun with hnsw ef_search up 2x and PQ codebook 128 -> 256? small search tweak might recover k recall without model changes.
jules: re-ran with ef_search=256, pq_codebook=256:
ci-bot: test-run 2056789678: embedding-eval/pelican-int8-hnsw-tweak -> completed
jules: ```
metrics:
  recall@1: 0.693
  recall@5: 0.892
  recall@10: 0.928
  silhouette(topic_clusters): 0.265
```
matt: recall@1 still ~3% below baseline but recall@5/10 close. silhouette similar.
sana: ok. next: can we check float16 non-quantized variant to separate quantization vs model capacity effects?
jules: running fp16 now, ETA ~10m.
ci-bot: test-run 2056790211: embedding-eval/pelican-fp16 -> completed
jules: ```
metrics:
  recall@1: 0.746
  recall@5: 0.895
  recall@10: 0.933
  silhouette(topic_clusters): 0.29
```
sana: interesting — fp16 recall@1 is slightly above prod baseline (0.746 vs 0.712 earlier?) wait comparing to baseline: baseline recall@1 (prod-512-fp16) = 0.745. pelican fp16 ~0.746 so parity. So major drop is quantization step.
matt: suggests trying per-channel int8 calibration with symmetric vs asymmetric codec. also try mixed-quant where embedding layer uses int8 but final projection stays fp16.
jules: did asymmetric per-channel int8 calibration (optimizer params from calibration set): recall@1 0.72, recall@5 0.89. better but not fully recovered.
alexa: for clustering, silhouette improved when using fp16. int8 reduces separation a bit but not catastrophic. maybe apply small temp-scaling on embeddings before L2 norm to correct distribution shift.
sana: good idea. can you try scale factor learned on calibration set? simple affine: x' = a*x + b where a,b chosen to match mean/norm distribution to baseline.
jules: ran scale fit -> a=1.08 b=-0.002 on calibration. test results:
ci-bot: test-run 2056790350: pelican-int8-calib-scale -> completed
jules: ```
metrics:
  recall@1: 0.734
  recall@5: 0.893
  recall@10: 0.929
  silhouette(topic_clusters): 0.279
```
sana: nice improvement. recall@1 now only ~1% under baseline. for rollout proposal: 1) ship pelican fp16 to staging for traffic tests, 2) enable int8 with scale-calib as experimental flag behind canary, 3) monitor recall@1 short-query and error rate.
matt: agree. add an eval checkpoint in CI to compare holdout recall delta per deploy (fail if delta > 3% for recall@1 on short_queries).
alexa: also add per-language thresholds; es shows higher sensitivity. maybe stricter canary for es-spike.
jules: I'll add eval hooks and a small script to compute and publish per-route recall deltas to console.
ci-bot: deploy-checklist updated: add canary flag pelican.int8.scale_calib, eval-hook id=embed-holdout-2056790400
sana: thanks team. I'll open a short doc in docs/embeddings with config defaults and the scale calibration snippet.
matt: small note — track tokenization diffs; pelican uses bytepair variant; ensure no tokenizer mismatch with downstream indexer.
sana: good call. we'll run a tokenizer roundtrip test next.
alexa: lgtm :thumbsup:
jules: ping when you want me to run longer-run recall@100 and brute-force NN to validate HNSW approximations.
sana: will do. closing thread for now, will update when staging runs start.
